raw_text: Beginning my professional journey eight years ago at a mid-sized industrial enterprise, I served as a Computer Vision Developer within a team of six. During this three-year tenure, I was primarily responsible for developing automated visual inspection systems using OpenCV 3.4 and Python 3.6 to identify defects in semiconductor manufacturing. I successfully implemented a custom filtering pipeline that increased throughput by twenty percent. Transitioning to a high-growth robotics startup, I spent three years as a Senior Vision Engineer leading a small squad of four specialists. I spearheaded the migration of our object detection models from standard CPU inference to NVIDIA Jetson hardware, utilizing C++ 14 and TensorRT to achieve a forty-five percent reduction in processing latency. My work involved optimizing YOLO-based architectures and integrating them with ROS for real-time navigation while providing technical mentorship to junior developers to ensure high code quality across the pipeline. For the past two years, I have acted as a Lead CV Architect at a specialized technology agency where I oversee a cross-functional team of eight. My current focus involves deploying robust multi-camera tracking systems using FastAPI 0.102 and PostgreSQL 15, managed through AWS ECS. I recently completed a project named VisionGuard which is an edge-based security system utilizing ONNX Runtime to process video streams with ninety-nine percent uptime. Another notable project is DeepSynth which uses generative models to create synthetic training data for rare edge cases in manufacturing. My next career direction is to transition into a Principal role focusing on the convergence of large vision models and embedded hardware. I hold a Master of Science in Robotics and Autonomous Systems which I completed in 2016. This academic background provided a foundation in spatial mathematics and sensor fusion that I apply daily in my engineering leadership.

raw_text: With a career spanning over seven years in the deep learning space, I currently serve as a Principal Machine Learning Engineer at a prominent robotics firm. My journey started seven and a half years ago at a large-scale software enterprise where I spent four years as a Research Engineer. In a team of ten, I focused on building scalable cloud-based vision APIs using PyTorch 1.8 and Flask, where I managed to reduce model training time from forty-eight hours to twelve hours by implementing distributed training across multiple GPUs. Following this, I joined a fast-paced autonomous delivery startup as a Tech Lead, managing a team of seven engineers for three and a half years. My primary responsibility was the end-to-end development of object detection and semantic segmentation pipelines for sidewalk navigation. I utilized YOLOv8 and integrated it with Triton Inference Server to handle over ten million inference requests daily with a ninety-eight percent success rate. I also pioneered a cost-saving initiative that reduced our AWS SageMaker expenditures by twenty-five percent through better spot instance utilization and model pruning. My project portfolio includes the development of OpenCV-Stream, a high-performance wrapper for low-latency RTSP processing, and NeuroLabel, an internal tool that uses active learning to prioritize data for human annotators. Currently, I am deepening my expertise in C++ 17 and CUDA kernels to further optimize inference on the edge. I am looking for a role that allows me to define the technical vision for large-scale AI products while remaining hands-on with architecture. I graduated with a Master of Computer Science in 2017, specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision. This formal education provided the theoretical underpinnings for my subsequent work in stochastic optimization and neural network compression techniques.
